messages.subject: [statnet_help] Edgecov and Dyadcov matrix / syntax specification
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Edgecov and Dyadcov matrix / syntax specification
messages.body_plain:
Hi-

I've been trying to use the edgecov / dyadcov terms in my models, and
have been encountering two problems. First, the models rarely, if
ever, run to completion, with frequent out of memory errors. Second,
when they do, the results do not make intuitive sense. This makes me
think that I'm not specifying the model correctly, and was hoping for
some assistance. I've searched the archives, but nothing seemed to
deal with my specific situation.

I have a network, with edge values. These values are distances between
pairs. The general syntax I've been using is this:

# dist.net is in edge-list format:
# id1, id2, distance,
# All distances >= 0, and the network is extremely sparse
# (~20K edges for 13.5K vertices)

edge <- read.csv('dist.net')
net <- network(edge[,1:2])

set.edge.value(net, "dist", dist[,3])
m1 <- ergm(net ~ edges + dyadcov(net, "dist"))

I haven't found any examples where an edge attribute of the same
network being modeled is used in edge/dyadcov. Is it possible to do
this?

Thanks!

MJH

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Dyad Statistics
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I know that the Summary statement produces summary statistics for the network, but is there a way to get statistics for each dyad? For instance, if I have Two-Path and GWDSP in my model, can I produce two vectors of length N*(N-1)/2 with
1) the number of 2-paths for each dyad, and
2) the number of shared partners for each dyad?

Thanks,
Sean

messages.subject: [statnet_help] components of a large network
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm trying to separate the components of a large network with approximately 250,000 vertices.

I understand that for a small network this can be achieved using the 'components' function from sna.

Does there exist an equivalent command suitable for large graphs?

Many thanks,
Brad
